findings.summary: build_features standardizes using mean/std of the whole DataFrame, and train.py calls it before train_test_split, leaking test statistics into training and making test AUC optimistic.

Mean and std are recomputed from whatever DataFrame is passed at inference, so a single row gives NaN std (all features NaN) and small batches are standardized against themselves, making predictions batch-dependent; fitted statistics are not persisted.
Constant (zero-variance) columns give std 0, so the division yields NaN/inf, which will make LogisticRegression raise.
